record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: Let A and B be PEPS tensors such that there exist epsilon greater than zero and a size L0 with the property that, for every L at least L0, the states they define on the L by L torus are within squared Hilbert-norm distance epsilon. Does this asymptotic closeness in the thermodynamic limit imply any local relation between A and B?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Projected Entangled Pair States (PEPS) tensor on the two-dimensional square lattice is a tensor $A \in \mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes (\mathbb{C}^{D})^{\otimes 4}$, where $d$ is the physical dimension and $D$ is the bond (virtual) dimension. For a positive integer $L$, the PEPS state $|\psi_L(A)\rangle$ on the $L \times L$ torus is defined by placing one copy of $A$ at each site of the $L\times L$ square lattice with periodic boundary conditions and contracting each pair of virtual indices along the edges of the lattice; the remaining physical indices give a vector in $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes L^2}$.

Two PEPS tensors $A$ and $B$ (with the same physical and bond dimensions) are said to be locally related if there exists an invertible (gauge) matrix $X \in GL(D,\mathbb{C})$ such that
$$B^{s}_{ijkl} = \sum_{i',j',k',l'} X_{ii'} X^{-1}_{j'j} X_{kk'} X^{-1}_{l'l}\, A^{s}_{i'j'k'l'},$$
or more generally if $A$ and $B$ are related by such a local intertwiner (possibly together with a permutation of the virtual indices arising from lattice symmetries).

Suppose $A$ and $B$ are PEPS tensors such that there exist $\varepsilon > 0$ and $L_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ with the following property: for every $L \geq L_0$,
$$\bigl\| \,|\psi_L(A)\rangle - |\psi_L(B)\rangle\,\bigr\|^2 \;\leq\; \varepsilon,$$
where the norms of $|\psi_L(A)\rangle$ and $|\psi_L(B)\rangle$ are normalized to one (or, equivalently, the squared Hilbert-space distance between the normalized states is at most $\varepsilon$).

Question: Does this asymptotic closeness in the thermodynamic limit imply any local relation between the tensors $A$ and $B$? More precisely, does it follow that $A$ and $B$ must be related (perhaps up to a small perturbation depending on $\varepsilon$) by a local gauge transformation on the virtual indices?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published resolution of this question. The problem concerns the rigidity of PEPS tensor representations under approximate equality of the states they generate in the thermodynamic limit; while exact-equality "fundamental theorem"-style results for normal/injective PEPS are known, the approximate analogue appears to remain open. No source claiming a proof or counterexample was found.

status_evidence.title: Locality at the Boundary Implies Gap in the Bulk for 2D PEPS
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses structural results for PEPS in the thermodynamic limit but does not address the approximate-equality rigidity question.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the approximate-equality question is reported.

status_evidence.title: A practical introduction to tensor networks: MPS and PEPS
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews PEPS gauge freedom and fundamental theorem for exact equality; approximate version not established.
status_evidence.claim: Only exact gauge equivalence results are reviewed.
